quote: But if I had to suggest an ur-mistake, it would be… well, I’ll let God say it for me:
content: The thesis, that suppression of criticism is the common factor in the great political killings, has support the essay does not cite and would have strengthened it. Sen's observation that no substantial famine has occurred in a functioning democracy with a free press, because governments that can be criticized are forced to respond, is the same claim made from the other side and backed by the comparative record of India after independence against China under Mao (Sen 1999, Development as Freedom, book, no DOI). The annotations to Human Evil and Muddled Thinking note that the Great Leap famine was an information catastrophe: cadres who reported true yields were purged, so the yields reported were false. That is a documented instance of the essay's mechanism, killing tens of millions, and it does not require Deuteronomy. The essay reached the right diagnosis and supported it with a scripture quotation and an analogy to nuclear fission.

quote: New Agers culturally inherit the cached thought that faith is positive, but lack Christianity’s exclusionary scripture to keep out competing memes. New Agers end up in happy death spirals around stars, trees, magnets, diets, spells, unicorns…
content: The sociology of religion found the opposite relation between exclusivity and fervor. Strict, exclusionary groups are the strong ones, because costly demands screen out free riders and raise members' commitment; low-cost, eclectic spirituality produces low commitment, high turnover and little collective action (Iannaccone 1994). New Age practice is the textbook case of the second type: pick-and-mix, consumerist, weakly organized, with adherents who drift between crystals and diets precisely because nothing binds them to any of it. That is not a death spiral; it is the absence of the conditions for one. The groups that go supercritical, in the essay's own examples, are the ones with scripture, membership and exit costs. The essay's model predicts that openness breeds fanaticism, and the data say that closure does.

quote: Bad argument gets counterargument. Does not get bullet. Never. Never ever never for ever.
content: This is right and it is the sequence's one injunction that the Fable annotations have no wish to qualify. It is worth noting only that the essay puts it in the same paragraph with the claim that there is "never an Idea so true that it's wrong to criticize any argument that supports it," and that the book in which both appear diagnoses its critics as motivated skeptics, sophisticated arguers, victims of the affect heuristic, cached-thought repeaters and residents of the Dark Side, in most cases without engaging their arguments. The rule is a good rule. Its author's practice, in this very book, is the softer form of the thing the rule forbids: not the bullet, but the diagnosis that makes counterargument unnecessary.
